## Technical Approach

The two options in the original record decide where a `/review` diagram suggestion lands, and the lens's own trigger settles it. Lens 3i-diagram fires only when a **persistent** diagram for the changed area is missing, so its finding is a documentation gap. An ephemeral-by-default placement (option a) would fill that gap with a scratch file and leave the gap open. A plain direct invocation already runs `/visualize`'s Step 3 persist-or-show-me question, offering "Save as a project doc" to `docs/diagrams/`, which is what a gap needs. `--source` is also documented as producer-only, set by a caller that invokes `/visualize` itself. `/review` only recommends a command for the user to run in wrap-up, so it was never a producer. Option b deletes a dead placement row and keeps the recommendation honest.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visualize/SKILL.md` — Used-by diagram, `--source` callers, placement table, Component-Skill Contract
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-doc-freshness-lens.md` — read-only check that the recommendation stays a direct invocation
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — `/visualize` section, `/review` row (line 635)

## Gotchas

- CLAUDE.md's Cross-references rule: every skill relationship is stated once, in `docs/skill-graph.md`. Removing the "caller" framing from `visualize/SKILL.md` must not leave a restated edge behind there.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s repo-wide item 4 ("Merged/closed PRs with local remnants") runs two queries, `gh pr list --state merged --limit 50` and `gh pr list --state closed --limit 50`, and justifies running both with a parenthetical:

> GitHub's PR `state` is `OPEN`/`CLOSED`/`MERGED` — mutually exclusive — so `--state closed` never overlaps `--state merged`

That claim is wrong for the CLI filter. `gh pr list --state closed` returns merged PRs too: in the 2026-10-21 sweep, 47 of the 50 `--state closed` entries were merged (e.g. #3891). The scan still produces correct rows only because each `headRefName` from either result is cross-checked against local branches, so a PR appearing in both lists is harmless.

The wrong note has a second, unstated cost. Because merged PRs fill most of the closed query's 50-entry window, "closed without merging" PRs get only a few of the slots (3 of 50 in that sweep). A stale local branch from an abandoned PR is therefore easily pushed out of view.

## Deliverables

1. Correct item 4's parenthetical so it states the real CLI behavior: `--state closed` includes merged PRs.
2. Make item 4's handling of the overlap explicit: either dedupe the two result sets by PR number in the procedure text, or select closed-without-merge PRs directly so the second query no longer spends its window on merged PRs. The plan records which and why.
3. If item 4's window behavior changes, keep the closed-without-merge coverage at least as wide as today's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Item 4's text no longer claims `--state closed` and `--state merged` are mutually exclusive, and states that the closed filter includes merged PRs.
- Item 4's procedure states how a PR present in both result sets is handled (deduped by number, or excluded by query shape).
- If the query shape changes, the closed-without-merge query's results contain only non-merged closed PRs (for example `gh pr list --state closed --json number,headRefName,mergedAt` filtered to `mergedAt == null`, or a search qualifier), verified by running the documented command against this repo and quoting its count in the PR.
- Any conformance test that pins item 4's prose (check `tests/` for `github-pr-scan` pins) passes after the edit, and `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Tidy's GitHub scan now describes its merged and closed PR queries correctly and finds stale branches from abandoned PRs more reliably.

## Technical Approach

This is a prose edit to item 4 in `github-pr-scan.md`, which is read through `compose-context.js` bundles under the `pr-scan` step. If Deliverable 2 changes the query, the cleanest shape is a single `gh pr list --state closed --limit {n} --json number,headRefName,mergedAt` call split locally into merged and closed-unmerged sets. That replaces two partially-overlapping queries with one, and widens the closed-unmerged window instead of shrinking it. The alternative (keep both queries, add an explicit dedupe sentence) is a smaller edit but keeps the window cost. The plan picks one and says why the other lost.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — repo-wide item 4 text and queries

## Gotchas

- `github-pr-scan.md` has transport-split rules: item 4 is PR-backed and degrades under the MCP transport. Keep the degrade note accurate if the query changes.
- Executable prose in `_shared/` may be byte-pinned by skill-prose conformance tests. Run the full suite after the edit.

## Original request

github-pr-scan item 4 wrongly treats the closed and merged PR lists as mutually exclusive

**Related:** none

Context: `gh pr list --state closed` also returns merged PRs (47 of 50 closed entries were merged in the 2026-10-21 sweep, e.g. #3891), so `_shared/github-pr-scan.md` repo-wide item 4's mutually-exclusive note is wrong; the scan works only because it dedupes by PR number.

Scope: correct the item 4 note and make the dedupe-by-number explicit (or filter the closed list by state).

Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (SDD final-review minor from #3846)

## Current State

All nine plugin-shipped routine templates (`plugin/skills/{backlog,code-health,dispatch,docs-health,harness-health,journey-health,release,specify,tidy}/routine-template.yml`) set `model: claude-sonnet-5-5` independently. `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js` (around line 92) asserts only that each `model` is a non-empty string. `_shared/routine-template-schema.md` (line 20) describes `model` as the "Default model for the routine's session", and the routine skill treats the live `session_context.model` as caller-overridable (`routine/SKILL.md`, the paragraph after Steps 0-9).

#3846 moved all nine from `claude-sonnet-5` to `claude-sonnet-5-5` by hand, bumping each `template_version`. A future migration that updates eight templates and misses the ninth would pass the suite unchanged. Its final whole-branch review raised this as a minor.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Ruling: a per-template `model` is a **supported, deliberate** choice (for example a heavier model for `release`), but it must be declared. A silent mismatch is a half-finished migration.
- [ ] In `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js`, replace the non-empty check with: one `ROUTINE_DEFAULT_MODEL` constant (today `claude-sonnet-5-5`) plus a `MODEL_OVERRIDES` map from template skill name to `{ model, reason }` (empty today). Every template's `model` must equal the default, or equal its own override entry. The test also fails on an override entry whose template no longer exists or whose model equals the default.
- [ ] Record the rule in `_shared/routine-template-schema.md`'s `model` row: shipped templates share one default model; a template that needs another adds an override entry with its reason; a model migration updates the default and every template in the same change

## Acceptance Criteria

- Changing one template's `model` to another value, with no override entry, fails the suite, and the failure names that template
- Adding a matching `MODEL_OVERRIDES` entry with a reason makes it pass
- A stale override entry (unknown template, or a model equal to the default) fails
- `_shared/routine-template-schema.md`'s `model` row states the shared-default-plus-declared-override rule
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

The original question was uniformity versus divergence. A plain uniformity assertion would forbid a choice the schema and the routine skill both allow, since the template value is only a caller-overridable default. Writing "divergence is allowed" into docs alone would leave the half-migration this record exists to catch undetected. A default plus an explicit override map does both: divergence is possible but must be stated with a reason in the one place a migration author edits, and anything undeclared fails. It needs no schema or parser change, so live routine records and `skills/routine/record-freshness.md`'s comparison are unaffected.

### Key Files

- `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js` — `ROUTINE_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `MODEL_OVERRIDES`, and the replaced assertion
- `plugin/skills/_shared/routine-template-schema.md` — `model` row (line 20)

## Gotchas

- The model profile table (`plugin/bin/lib/model-profiles/profiles.js`) uses aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`), while routine templates pin versioned ids, so it is not a drop-in source for the default; keep the constant in the test.
- Keep the failure message naming the template and its value, so the next migration author sees exactly which file was missed.

## Original request

Decide whether shipped routine templates must share one model value

Origin: ledger resolve gate (SDD final-review minor from #3846)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

All nine shipped routine templates under `plugin/skills/*/routine-template.yml` pin `model:` independently, and `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js:92` asserts only that each value is a non-empty string. #3846 moved all nine from `claude-sonnet-5` to `claude-sonnet-5-5` by hand, bumping each `template_version`. Nothing in the suite would fail if a future model migration updated eight templates and missed the ninth: the half-migrated tree would pass. The #3846 final whole-branch review raised this as a minor.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide whether the shipped templates must all share one `model` value, or whether per-template divergence (for example a heavier model for `release`) is a supported case.
- [ ] If they must share one value, add the assertion to `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js`; if they may diverge, record that in `plugin/skills/_shared/routine-template-schema.md` so the next migration does not re-raise it.

## Open Question

Must every plugin-shipped routine template share a single `model` value? The answer is a product call: a uniformity assertion forbids a per-routine model choice that the schema does not currently forbid.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `tests/routine-template-schema.test.js` — possible all-templates-share-one-model assertion
- `plugin/skills/_shared/routine-template-schema.md` — state whether per-template model divergence is supported
